items.topic: Mission Control vertical slice scene depth
items.context: Round-1 D1 resolved to 'C — full vertical slice': Mission Control gets a real Ground Control theme + real R3F scene + real data fetch through to gap badges, while the other 5 routes get trivial placeholder scenes. The plan now commits to a starfield + a few satellite-node meshes as the Mission Control scene. That's one plausible interpretation, but 'full vertical slice' leaves room for a bigger or smaller scene. We need to lock this so theming-engine's later work on Mission Control visuals doesn't collide with or overwrite the scaffold's slice.

options.label: Minimal real scene — starfield only
options.rationale: Just an instanced-points starfield tinted with the Ground Control accent color. No satellites, no orbits, no chart. Smallest surface area; theming-engine adds satellites/orbits when it fills the Mission Control visual.

options.label: Starfield + satellite nodes (recommended)
options.rationale: Instanced-points starfield + 3-5 rotating satellite node meshes wired to the Ground Control palette. Modest R3F surface (fits on a single screen of code), exercises both static (stars) and animated (satellites) rendering, enough to validate perf-tier hooks. Theming-engine can still add orbital lines, mission data overlays, refined materials without overwriting scene structure.

options.label: Starfield + satellites + live metric visualization
options.rationale: B plus: a small Recharts/R3F metric visualization tied to one of the live metrics from /api/v1/dashboards/mission-control (e.g. 'active scenarios' as a number+trend). Proves data-to-visual binding but blurs the line with theming-engine which owns visualization design.

options.rationale: Provide a different Mission Control scene depth in the freeform field.

items.context: Round-1 D5 freeform: 'Change to bas/ e2e standard other scenarios use (gets powered by test-genie scenario that calls browser-automation-studio). Should be a guide somewhere to set it up.' Research confirmed the pattern: `bas/actions/`, `bas/flows/`, `bas/cases/01-foundation/` etc., `bas/registry.json` generated by `test-genie registry build`, `.vrooli/testing.json` toggles `playbooks.enabled`. The remaining question is scope: how many cases do we ship in the scaffold vs. leave for sibling items?

options.label: Bare minimum — 1 smoke case
options.rationale: One case: `/` loads without console errors. Theming-engine and kiosk-ux each add their own cases. Tightest scope, but leaves the 6-route navigation and gap-badge rendering untested at e2e level — those are scaffold seams, so not ideal.

options.label: Per-route load cases + Mission Control gap badge (recommended)
options.rationale: 1 action (navigate-to-route) + 1 flow (navigate-all-routes) + 6 route-load cases (page loads, data-theme set, no console errors) + 1 Mission Control gap-badges case. All under `bas/cases/01-foundation/`. Validates the scaffold's actual seams: routing, theme wrapper, gap badge rendering on the reference slice. ~7 cases total — manageable and directly tied to scaffold DoD. Matches the pattern in `scenario-completeness-scoring/bas/`.

options.label: Full foundation — per-route cases + data shape assertions
options.rationale: B plus: cases that assert each route displays at least one metric pulled from /api/v1/dashboards/{id}, plus a gaps-endpoint visibility case. Pushes into behavior that could equally live in integration tests; more coverage overlap without a clear scaffold-specific win.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different BAS case scope in the freeform field.

items.topic: Port allocation for API and UI
items.context: Scanning `scenarios/*/.vrooli/service.json` shows the current port landscape: 15xxx cluster (API: 15000, 15010, 15050, 15100, 18600, 18710, 18800), 36xxx cluster (UI: 36110, 36221-36242, 36300, 36400). The plan must commit to specific ports in Phase 1 to avoid downstream rework. Static ports are preferred (consistent with siblings like web-console :36233, swarm-manager :36234).

options.label: API 15200 / UI 36243 (recommended)
options.rationale: 15200 sits cleanly in the 15xxx API cluster with a 100-port gap above the current max (15100), leaving room for neighboring scenarios. 36243 is the next free slot in the contiguous 36221–36242 block. Both confirmed free by `rg '"port":\s*\d+' scenarios/*/.vrooli/service.json`. Matches the sibling convention.

options.label: API 18900 / UI 36500
options.rationale: 18900 sits in the 18xxx cluster (used by agent-manager 18800, prd-control-tower 18600, git-control-tower 18710) with a 100-port gap. 36500 sits beyond git-control-tower's 36400, suggesting a new sub-cluster for command-center + future related scenarios. Slightly more room to grow but breaks the contiguous 36xxx layout.

options.label: API 25200 / UI 36243
options.rationale: 25xxx cluster (currently only agent-manager 25100) for the API side; UI stays at 36243. Emphasizes that command-center is a different class of service (pure aggregator). Cleanest separation but splits a small cluster further.

options.rationale: Provide different port choices in the freeform field.

items.freeform: Use the standard ranges from the scenario template (react-vite)

items.context: Finding 6 settled a file-based JSON registry loaded at API startup. Round-1 D3 resolved to populating all 6 dashboards with real metrics. With full population, the registry becomes a meaningful source of truth — a malformed entry would cause silent miscounting of gaps or broken dashboard payloads. The plan commits to validation, but the strategy is TBD. Options range from trust-the-file to a strict schema library.

options.label: Trust unmarshalling, no explicit validation
options.rationale: Go struct tags enforce shape; no extra validation. Fastest to implement; but enum values (`dataSource`, `upstreamSource`) aren't enforced, duplicate metric IDs aren't caught, and required-field-ness depends on JSON zero-values — brittle.

options.label: Hand-written validation pass, fail-fast on startup (recommended)
options.rationale: Unmarshal into typed structs, then iterate: require `id`, `label`, `dataSource`, `upstreamSource`; enum-check the latter two; reject duplicate metric IDs within a dashboard; reject dashboard keys outside the canonical 6. On failure, log error + os.Exit(1). No external deps, full control over error messages, catches every class of registry bug. Matches Go-idiomatic validation in sibling scenarios.

options.label: External JSON Schema library (e.g. xeipuuv/gojsonschema)
options.rationale: Ship a `.schema.json` file alongside the registry and validate at startup with a library. More reusable if the schema is consumed elsewhere (e.g. an IDE autocomplete config); heavier dep surface and more config boilerplate for a single-producer, single-consumer file.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide a different validation strategy in the freeform field.

items.text: BAS/test-genie setup confirmed. Pattern across siblings (e.g. `scenarios/scenario-completeness-scoring/bas/`, `scenarios/browser-automation-studio/bas/`): per-scenario `bas/` directory with `actions/`, `flows/`, `cases/01-foundation/` through `06-nonfunctional/`, `seeds/`, and a generated `registry.json`. `.vrooli/testing.json` controls phase enablement via `playbooks.enabled` (default `false` in most siblings — we'll set it to `true`). `make test` routes through `vrooli scenario test`, which invokes `test-genie execute`, which runs the playbooks phase via BAS. No separate Playwright install/config needed. Reference: `scenarios/test-genie/docs/guides/end-to-end-example.md` and `scenarios/browser-automation-studio/bas/README.md`.

plan_updates: Round 2 incorporated round-1 resolutions throughout plan.md. Purpose/problem/scope sections now commit to Mission Control as a full vertical slice with placeholder peers; Required Reading adds browser-automation-studio and e2e-testing skills; Technical Context locks ports (15200/36243), gap-registry validation approach, r3f-stats storage model, and LPBS client shape; Phases 1-6 restructured so Phase 3 fully populates the registry + validates it + wires the LPBS client with fallback, Phase 4 ships the Mission Control scene + placeholder scene split, Phase 5 replaces the Playwright path with a BAS/test-genie setup (1 action + 1 flow + 7 cases under `bas/cases/01-foundation/`); Contracts section documents the BAS case taxonomy; Risks section adds BAS setup risk + LPBS-untestable mitigation; DoD items now cover every resolved decision plus the new slice/testing commitments. Remaining TBDs in this round target: Mission Control scene depth (d1), BAS case coverage scope (d2), specific port choices (d3), validation strategy (d4). Readiness is currently drafted at 3/3/3/3/3 in the plan.md state, but will only be *binding* once d1-d4 resolve; unresolved decisions here are scope/depth dial choices rather than foundational unknowns.
